What looks like free choice in Mephisto (novel) is older than choice itself. Mephisto was first published in 1936 by an Exilliteratur firm based in Amsterdam, while the author was in self-imposed exile from the Hitler regime. It was published for the first time in Germany in the East Berlin Aufbau-Verlag in 1956.

Nobody designed the part of Mephisto (novel) you experience — it was inherited. Klaus Mann fled to exile in March 1933 to avoid political persecution by Hitler's regime. In Amsterdam he worked for the exile magazine Die Sammlung, which attacked National Socialism.

Every serious account of Mephisto (novel) eventually collides with the question of who is deciding. His friend and publisher Fritz Helmut Landshoff made him a "relatively generous offer", as Mann wrote to his mother on 21 July 1935. Mann originally intended to write a utopian novel about Europe in 200 years.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Mephisto (novel) — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. However, Mann discarded this idea stating that he could not write an apolitical novel at that point in history. The author Hermann Kesten suggested that he write a novel of a homosexual careerist in the Third Reich, with the director of the state theatre Gustaf Gründgens as a subject matter.

The selfish-gene reading of Mephisto (novel) makes it less romantic and far more precise. In 1924, Klaus Mann, his sister Erika, Gründgens, and Pamela Wedekind had all worked together on a stage production of Mann's Anja und Esther and had toured through Germany. Gründgens and Erika Mann got engaged while Klaus Mann similarly got engaged to Wedekind.

Freud is not dead; he is simply no longer allowed to be the whole answer. The first two got married in 1926 but divorced in 1929 and Wedekind married writer Carl Sternheim a year later. Gründgens and Mann had both belonged in the early 1930s to a strongly left-wing theatre group that in January 1933 was touring Spain.

The feeling that Mephisto (novel) means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. When Hitler became German Chancellor on 30 January 1933, the group was in Madrid, and Mann urged Gründgens not to return to Germany. When Gründgens disregarded Mann's advice and not only returned to Germany, but embraced the Nazi regime (for purely opportunistic reasons), Mann never forgave his former friend Gründgens.

Nothing in Mephisto (novel) was built for you — it was built for reproduction. Klaus Mann was exiled in 1934; Gründgens became a renowned theater and movie director in Nazi Germany. Although he attacked Gründgens in newspaper articles, Mann hesitated to use homosexuality as a theme in the novel as he himself was gay and decided to use "negroid masochism" as the main character's sexual preference.

The psychology underneath Mephisto (novel) is simpler and older than the story on top. After the novel's publication in 1936, the newspaper Pariser Tageszeitung presented it as a roman à clef. Mann resented this characterization and argued that he had not written about a particular individual, but about a type of individual.

Behind Mephisto (novel) sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. The novel portrays actor Hendrik Höfgen's rise from the Hamburger Künstlertheater (Hamburg Artists' Theater) in 1926 to nationwide fame in 1936. Initially, Höfgen flees to Paris on receiving news of the Nazis' rise to power because of his communist past (learning from a friend that he is on a blacklist).

The nihilist does not deny Mephisto (novel) — he only refuses to flatter it. A former co-actress from Hamburg, Angelika Siebert, travels to Berlin to convince Lotte von Lindenthal, the girlfriend (and later wife) of a Luftwaffe general, to have him pardoned. On returning to Berlin he quickly manages to win over Lotte and her general, and with his support has a wonderful career.

What culture calls destiny in Mephisto (novel) is usually just selection pressure wearing a suit. On obtaining the role of Mephisto in Faust Part One he realizes that he actually made a pact with evil (i.e. Nazism) and lost his humane values (even denouncing his mistress as "Black Venus").

There are situations where Höfgen tries to help his friends or tell the prime minister about concentration camp hardships, but he is always concerned not to lose his Nazi patrons. The Prussian Ministerpräsident (Prime Minister) celebrates his 43rd birthday in 1936 in the Berliner Opernhaus (Berlin Opera House).

Take away the meaning and Mephisto (novel) still functions — that is the disturbing part. The party is so magnificent and extravagant that the foreign guests feel intimidated. As the propaganda minister enters the hall, his presence creates a stir.

The story then reverts to the mid-1920s: Hendrik Höfgen, Otto Ulrichs and Hans Miklas belong to the Hamburger Künstlertheater (Artists' Theatre in Hamburg).

The bleak reading of Mephisto (novel) is also the most testable one. Höfgen currently works there as an actor and director, and is friends with Otto Ulrichs, as they incessantly plan a "revolutionary theatre." The Hamburger Künstlertheater is the first rung on Höfgen's career ladder. He works there 16 hours a day and often suffers from fits of excitement and nerves.

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Mephisto (novel). When the Berlin actress Dora Martin has a guest performance, he hides in her dressing room. Hans Miklas, a follower of the NSDAP, talks negatively of Martin because of her Jewish origin.

The self that experiences Mephisto (novel) is a committee, not a king. In a harbour pub in Hamburg, he gets to know Juliette Martins. Her father is an engineer from Hamburg and her mother was African, giving Juliette her dark skin.

Reproduction explains more of Mephisto (novel) than any philosophy dares to admit. Juliette is the only person he allows to address him as Heinz – not even his family are allowed this. Höfgen is introduced to Barbara Bruckner (the daughter of Geheimrat Bruckner) by his colleague Nicoletta von Niebuhr.

Once you see Mephisto (novel) as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Nicoletta joins them and is visited almost daily by the eccentric writer Theophil Marder. Theophil Marder writes Nicoletta a telegram, saying that his feelings are hurt by his marriage; a wife must belong to her husband regardless of circumstances.

The story Mephisto (novel) tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Nicoletta von Niebuhr travels straight to him and gives up her job. He receives his place there on the recommendation of Dora Martin, Geheimrat Bruckner and Theophil Marder.

Meaning is not found in Mephisto (novel) — it is manufactured for it. He leaves the Hamburger Künstlertheater after an argument with Hans Miklas, after he called Lotte Lindenthal a blonde cow. Through the support of Dora Martin, Höfgen receives a role in the State Theatre in Berlin.

The cold light on Mephisto (novel) leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Now he spends a week at the Reichskanzlerplatz (Chancellor of the Reich) and learns to drive. Geheimrat Bruckner and his daughter Barbara come to Berlin less and less often and withdraw from Höfgen.

Mephisto (novel) did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. In 1932, "Faust" is included in the play's performance listings to commemorate 100 years since the death of Goethe. Höfgen takes the role of Mephisto, which becomes his most successful part.

The honest version of Mephisto (novel) starts by giving up the comforting part. Höfgen can hardly believe that the Nazis will come to power, but on 30 January 1933, Hitler is named as the new Reichskanzler (Chancellor of the Reich). Once the shooting in Spain is finished, Höfgen doesn't return to Germany, instead travelling to Paris, because he had been warned that he was on the Nazi blacklist.

Strip Mephisto (novel) of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. After his colleague from Hamburg Angela Siebert puts in a good word for him with Lotte Lindenthal, Lotte decides to choose him as her partner for her debut performance at the Berlin State Theatre. Höfgen therefore is under the protection of the Ministerpräsident and can return to Germany. "Faust" is again written in the performance listings of the State Theatre.

Thanks to his patron, he organises the release of Otto Ulrichs, whom the Nazis had imprisoned in a concentration camp for his communist beliefs. Meanwhile, Hans Miklas feels betrayed by national socialism, since in his opinion it was of no benefit to Germany.

What looks like free choice in Mephisto (novel) is older than choice itself. Höfgen wants the Nazis to know nothing of his relationship with the dark-skinned Juliette. Since Juliette refuses, Höfgen finds no alternative but to allow Juliette to be arrested.

The Ministerpräsident wants Höfgen to take the post and the propaganda minister disagrees, but eventually gives in.
